relations.subject: cbl:sql-plus-plus-mobile
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - direct match to the promoted isSynonymOf shape
relations.evidence: N1QL is Couchbase's implementation of the developing SQL++ standard. As such the terms N1QL and SQL++ are used interchangeably in Couchbase documentation unless explicitly stated otherwise.

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-scoping
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted relation, applied across the product-family axis (CBL vs. Server) rather than an edition/version axis
relations.evidence: USE KEYS | SELECT fname, email FROM tutorial USE KEYS ["dave", "ian"]; | SELECT fname, email FROM tutorial WHERE meta().id IN ("dave", "ian");

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-set-operations
relations.evidence: NEST | SELECT * FROM `user` u NEST orders orders ON KEYS ARRAY s.order_id FOR s IN u.order_history END; | NEST is not supported ... UNION, INTERSECT, and EXCEPT | All three are supported (with ALL and DISTINCT variants) | Not supported

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-join-support
relations.evidence: OUTER JOIN | Both LEFT and RIGHT OUTER JOIN supported | Only LEFT OUTER JOIN supported (and necessary for query expressability)

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-comparison-operators
relations.evidence: <, <=, =, etc. operators | Can compare either complex values or scalar values | Only scalar values may be compared

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-order-by
relations.evidence: ORDER BY | Result sequencing is based on specific rules described in SQL++ (server) OrderBy clause | Result sequencing is based on the SQLite ordering described in SQLite select overview

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-select-distinct
relations.evidence: SELECT DISTINCT | Supported | SELECT DISTINCT VALUE is supported when the returned values are scalars

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-crud
relations.evidence:
SQL++ for Mobile only supports Read or Query operations.

SQL++ for Server fully supports CRUD operation.

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-boolean-logic
relations.evidence: In SQL++ for Mobile — unlike SQL++ for Server — NULL is implicitly converted to FALSE before evaluating logical operations.

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-division-operator
relations.evidence: SQL++ for Server always performs float division regardless of the types of the operands. You can force this behavior in SQL++ for Mobile by using the DIV(x, y) function.

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-round-function
relations.evidence: SQL++ for Server ROUND() uses the _Rounding to Nearest Even_ convention (for example, ROUND(1.85) returns 1.8). You can force this behavior in Couchbase Lite by using the ROUND_EVEN() function.

relations.subject: cbl:sql-mobile-division-operator
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted relation fits: use DIV()/ROUND_EVEN() to force Server-equivalent behavior in Mobile
relations.evidence: You can force this behavior in SQL++ for Mobile by using the DIV(x, y) function.

cross_product_finding: This is the single most important page in the batch for testing whether the vocabulary crosses product families: it explicitly, tabularly names Couchbase Server's SQL++ features (Scopes/Collections addressing, USE KEYS/ON KEYS/ON KEY, NEST/LEFT OUTER NEST, UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT, OUTER JOIN variants, comparison-operator value-typing, ORDER BY sequencing rules, SELECT DISTINCT, CREATE INDEX, INSERT/UPSERT/DELETE, boolean three-valued logic, division, ROUND) and states a mobile-vs-server behavior difference for each. Structurally, every single row is a clean fit for the already-promoted 'behavesDifferentlyUnder' relation - but the axis of variation is the *product family* itself (CBL/SQLite-backed engine vs. Couchbase-Server/its own query engine), not an edition or version as in prior rounds. We could not literally reuse a server/ concept id for the 'SQL++ for Server' side of each comparison because the given registry contains no statement-level server/ concepts (only privilege:query-manage-index, editions, versions, index-state) - we minted a single stub concept (cbl:server-sql-plusplus-dialect) to stand in for the whole family and flagged it for coordinator reconciliation. Substantively: SQL++ for Mobile is read/query-only (no CREATE INDEX, no INSERT/UPSERT/DELETE at all - a much larger restriction than any RBAC privilege denial in server/, since it's not deniable/grantable, it's simply absent from the client engine), and its boolean/arithmetic semantics inherit from SQLite rather than from Couchbase's own N1QL evaluator, which is a purely engine-implementation-driven divergence with no access-control or licensing dimension at all.
